To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the regio- (and stereo)selectivity of the silyl- or stannylcuprating reaction of alkynes bearing a N- or S- functional group can be controlled by the nature of the metal, and that the regiochemistry of the subsequent reaction of the vinyl metal species with a wide range (of electrophiles can be controlled by changing the reaction conditions.

the reaction of alkynes bearing functional groups with organometallic reagents in a metal-mediated fashion is a powerful and general route to a wide range of polysubstituted olefinic systems, including di-, tri- and tetrasubstitued alkenes.

the development and application of new synthetic methodologies for the regio- stereoselective construction of polyfunctionalized olefins.

the synthesis of polysubstituted olefinic frameworks through the regio- stereoselective addition of silyl- and/or stannylcuprates to alkynes bearing functional groups at one or both termini of the alkyne moiety and the subsequent functionalization of the resulting vinylmetal species with a variety of electrophiles.
the development of new synthetic methodologies for the preparation of polysubstituted aliphatic alkenes.

the regio- stereoselective construction of trisubstutited alkenes is still a major challenge and the development of new methods for this purpose is a very active area of research.
the synthesis of tri-substituted al-kenes is still an unsolved problem.4 The same can be said for the preparation of tetra- and pentasubstituted alkanes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a general and highly regio- and/or stereoselective method for the synthesis and functionalization of trisub- and tetrasubstitu- ted alkenes by metal-mediated silylation or stannylation of alkynes followed by displacement of the vinylmetal fragment with various electrophiles.
the regio- stereoselective formation of polysubstituted aliphatic olefins is possible by metal-mediated reactions, in particular, by cuprate and Pd(0)-catalyzed reactions.
we have developed an efficient and general method to prepare a wide variety of tri- and even tetrasubstitued olefins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

vinylsilanes and vinylstannanes, which are readily available by silyl- or stannylcuprations of alkynes, can be used as versatile intermediates for the preparation of a wide variety of polysubstituted alkanes and alkenes, including tri-and tetrasubstitut ed alkenes, in high yield, with good to excellent regio- and/or stereoselectivity.

the use of organometallic reagents in combination with a wide range (and sometimes even a variety) of electrophiles allows for the preparation of a variety of polysubstituted aliphatic alkenes in a regio-and stereocontrolled fashion.
the use of organometallic species in a regio-and stereoselective manner can be a very powerful and flexible tool for the preparation of a large variety of polysubstituted olefin derivatives.
